findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type and does not normalize user identifier, causing cross-identity collisions
findings.body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` in `Check` is constructed using the raw `checkReq.UserUID` from `types.ParseTypeID(subject)` without including `checkReq.IdentityType` or normalizing user IDs via `GetUserIdentifiers` (unlike `permCache`, which resolves `userIdentifiers.UID`). Because subjects can be `anonymous:0`, `render:0`, `user:<id_or_uid>`, or `service-account:<id_or_uid>`, two problems occur:
1. If an anonymous check (`subject = "anonymous:0"`) is denied for a resource, `permDenialKey` is cached with `UserUID = "0"`. A subsequent check for `render:0` on the same resource will hit this denial cache entry and be falsely denied.
2. If a user or service account is checked by numeric ID (`user:42`) and denied, and is later checked by UID (`user:uid42`), or vice versa, they produce different denial cache keys.

Include the identity type (or canonical subject) and the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID` when building `permDenialKey`.

findings.title: Cached folder tree is not refreshed on permission cache miss, breaking access to newly created nested folders/dashboards
findings.body: The goal of this PR is to allow users to access newly created dashboards and folders by falling back to the database when the cached permissions do not grant access. However, on the fallback path in `Check`, `getIdentityPermissions` refreshes `permCache` from the DB, and then `checkPermission` -> `checkInheritedPermissions` -> `buildFolderTree` still reads from `s.folderCache` without bypassing it. If a user has permission on a parent folder (`folders:uid:parent`), creates a subfolder `child` inside `parent`, and then creates or accesses a dashboard inside `child` while `folderCache` is already populated, `tree.Ancestors("child")` will not find `parent` in the stale cached folder tree, `checkPermission` will return `false`, and that denial will then be written into `permDenialCache` for `shortCacheTTL` (30s).

findings.title: Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets permCache value to false instead of true
findings.body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` / `Should deny on explicit cache deny entry`, line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` with the comment `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`. Because the map value is `false` (and no fakeStore permissions are configured), `s.Check` would return `Allowed: false` even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored. The map value should be `true` to actually verify that `permDenialCache` takes precedence over `permCache`.
